etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English wild, wilde, from Old English wilde, from Proto-West Germanic *wilþī, from Proto-Germanic *wilþijaz, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂welh₁- (“hair, wool, grass, ear (of corn), forest”).

definitions.definition: Untamed; not domesticated; specifically, in an unbroken line of undomesticated animals (as opposed to feral, referring to undomesticated animals whose ancestors were domesticated).

quote.citation: c. 1527–1542, Thomas Wyatt, “Who so list to hounte”, in Egerton MS 2711‎[1], page 7v:
quote.text: noli me tangere for Ceſars I ameand wylde for to hold though I ſeme tame

quote.citation: c. 1603–1606, William Shakespeare, “The Tragedie of King Lear”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act II, scene iv]:
quote.text: Winter's not gone yet, if the wild geese fly that way.

quote.citation: 1637, John Milton, “Lycidas”, in Poems of Mr. John Milton, […], London:  […]  Ruth Raworth for Humphrey Mosely, […], published 1646, →OCLC, page 58:
quote.text: Thee Shepherd, thee the Woods, and deſert caves, / With wilde Thyme and the gadding Vine o'regrown,

quote.citation: 1950 July, “Traveller's Joy”, in Railway Magazine, page ii (advertisement):
quote.text: Their flowers range from the rather formal blossoming of outer London to the wilder flowering of the country, where willow-herb and broom, traveller's joy and campion, go rioting over the chalky banks of the Metropolitan Line.

quote.citation: 2013 May–June, David Van Tassel, Lee DeHaan, “Wild Plants to the Rescue”, in American Scientist, volume 101, number 3:
quote.text: Plant breeding is always a numbers game. […] The wild species we use are rich in genetic variation, and individual plants are highly heterozygous and do not breed true. In addition, we are looking for rare alleles, so the more plants we try, the better.

definitions.definition: From or relating to wild creatures.
Unrestrained or uninhibited.

quote.citation: 1850, [Alfred, Lord Tennyson], In Memoriam, London: Edward Moxon, […], →OCLC, Prologue:
quote.text: Forgive these wild and wandering cries,⁠Confusions of a wasted youth;⁠Forgive them where they fail in truth,And in thy wisdom make me wise.

definitions.definition: Raucous, unruly, or licentious.

quote.citation: 2022 August 10, Philip Haigh, “Scotland switched on to electrification”, in RAIL, number 963, page 35:
quote.text: Those most rural routes will not get overhead wires. As Reeve told the seminar: "Even in my wildest dreams, I can't see a business case for electrifying the Far North Line."

definitions.definition: (electrical engineering) Of unregulated and varying frequency.
Visibly and overtly anxious; frantic.

quote.citation: 2011 August 7, Chris Bevan, “Man City 2-3 Man Utd”, in BBC Sport:
quote.text: City, in contrast, were lethargic in every area of the pitch and their main contribution in the first half-hour was to keep referee Phil Dowd busy, with Micah Richards among four of their players booked early on, in his case for a wild lunge on Young.

definitions.definition: Furious; very angry.
Disheveled, tangled, or untidy.
Enthusiastic.
Very inaccurate; far off the mark.
Exposed to the wind and sea; unsheltered.
(nautical, of a vessel) Hard to steer.
(mathematics, of a knot) Not capable of being represented as a finite closed polygonal chain.
(slang) Amazing, awesome, unbelievable.
Able to stand in for others, e.g. a card in games, or a text character in computer pattern matching.

quote.citation: 2009, Leonardo Vanneschi, Steven Gustafson, Alberto Moraglio, Genetic Programming: 12th European Conference:
quote.text: We define a pattern as a valid GP subtree that might contain wild characters [i.e. wildcards] in any of its nodes.

In this card game, aces are wild: they can take the place of any other card.

definitions.definition: Of an audio recording: intended to be synchronized with film or video but recorded separately.
Inaccurately; not on target.
(of an audio recording) Intended to be synchronized with film or video but recorded separately.
(singular, with "the") The undomesticated state of a wild animal.
(chiefly in the plural) A wilderness.

quote.text: Thus every good his native wilds impartImprints the patriot passion on his heart;And e’en those ills that round his mansion riseEnhance the bliss his scanty funds supplies.

definitions.definition: (intransitive, slang) To commit random acts of assault, robbery, and rape in an urban setting, especially as a gang.

quote.citation: 1989 April 22, David E. Pitt, “Jogger's Attackers Terrorized at Least 9 in 2 Hours”, in New York Times, page 1:
quote.text: ...Chief of Detectives Robert Colangelo, who said the attacks appeared unrelated to money, race, drugs, or alcohol, said that some of the 20 youths brought in for questioning has told investigators that the crime spree was the product of a pastime called "wilding"."It's not a term that we in the police had heard before," the chief said, noting that the police were unaware of any similar incident in the park recently. "They just said, 'We were going wilding.' In my mind at this point, it implies that they were going to raise hell."...

quote.citation: 1999, Busta Rhymes (Trevor Taheim Smith, Jr.), Iz They Wildin Wit Us? (song)
quote.text: Now is they wildin with us / And getting rowdy with us.

definitions.definition: (intransitive, slang) (In the form wilding or wildin') To act in a strange or unexpected way.

quote.citation: 2021 April 6, Shirley Ju, “The New Voice of Brooklyn is Here To 'Drench 'Em'”, in Flaunt Magazine‎[2], archived from the original on 7 September 2022:
quote.text: They had a big influence on me. They had a big influence on Brooklyn period. I like the nonsense. [laughs] They were wildin'. Everyone in Brooklyn was liking that shit. They're wildin'.  Their story in the stu, it gets deep.

quote.citation: 2021 October 14, Jack Beresford, “Hospital Security Guard 'Heartbroken' After Being Fired Over Viral Video Confrontation”, in Newsweek‎[3]:
quote.text: Kinsey posted a clip of the incident alongside a caption that reads: "Damn the ER in Tulsa be wildin'."

quote.citation: 2022 April 20, A. Sherrod Blakely, “The Neverending Disappointment of Kyrie Irving”, in Bleacher Report‎[4]:
quote.text: The Ringer's Culture/NBA writer Wosney Lambre said it best: "I think it's a bad look for the players to be wilding on the fans like this. Fair or not, the players are held to a higher standard of decorum than the loser fans. It is what it is."

definitions.definition: Alternative form of weald
